content: 1. On the first day of treatment, administer 5 mL of posaconazole orally twice daily. Subsequently, administer 100 mg orally once daily for 13 days. 2. For patients refractory to itraconazole and/or fluconazole, administer 400 mg (10 mL) of posaconazole orally twice daily. The duration of treatment should be determined based on the severity of the underlying disease and the clinical response. 3. Posaconazole is indicated for the treatment of invasive aspergillosis and zygomycosis. 4. Posaconazole is also indicated for the prophylaxis of invasive Aspergillus and Candida infections in patients at high risk due to severe immunocompromise, such as hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients with graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) or patients with hematologic malignancies experiencing prolonged neutropenia from chemotherapy. 5. The oral suspension form of posaconazole is indicated for the treatment of oropharyngeal candidiasis. 6. The safety and efficacy of posaconazole in patients under 13 years of age have not been established. 7. Posaconazole and alfuzosin both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 8. Posaconazole and asenapine both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 9. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Posaconazole and buprenorphine (buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, or long-acting injection) both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 11. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Posaconazole and ceritinib both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 13. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Concomitant use of conivaptan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 16. Posaconazole and crizotinib both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 17. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine (oral or intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Posaconazole and efavirenz both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 19. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 20. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated with eliglustat in poor or intermediate metabolizers. In extensive metabolizers, reduce the eliglustat dose from 84 mg twice daily to 84 mg once daily. Eliglustat is contraindicated if strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors are used concomitantly with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 21. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ergoloid mesylates by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 22. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 23. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration of flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 25. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 26. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ivabradine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration of ivabradine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 28. Posaconazole increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it significantly increases lomitapide levels, leading to potential toxicities. 29. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 30. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the increased risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 31. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration of lurasidone with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 32. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it may lead to heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. 33. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of methylergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 34. Posaconazole and mirtazapine both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 35. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it may precipitate opioid withdrawal symptoms. 36. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 37. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 38. Posaconazole increases the levels of regorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it increases regorafenib levels while decreasing exposure to its active metabolites, M-2 and M-5. 39. Ribociclib increases the toxicity of posaconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 40. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated due to the increased risk of rhabdomyolysis. 41. Posaconazole and sunitinib both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 42. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used after the ramp-up phase, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 75%. 43. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of venlafaxine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 44. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 45. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A inhibitor is necessary, temporarily interrupt acalabrutinib treatment. 46. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of adagrasib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors until adagrasib concentrations reach steady-state (~8 days). 47. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration as it may increase DM1 exposure and toxicity. 48. Posaconazole increases the levels of afatinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce the afatinib dose by 10 mg if not tolerated when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. 49. Posaconazole and amiodarone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 50. Posaconazole and amisulpride both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 51. Posaconazole and anagrelide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 52. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong dual inhibitors of CYP3A4 and P-gp. 53. Posaconazole and aripiprazole both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 54. Posaconazole and arsenic trioxide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 55. Posaconazole and artemether both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 56. Posaconazole and asenapine transdermal both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 57. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration as it may lead to severe adverse events, including hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. 58. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 59. Posaconazole increases the levels of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. 60. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefit outweighs the risk. 61. Posaconazole increases the levels of bosutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration as it increases bosutinib plasma concentration by approximately fivefold. 62. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by 50%. After discontinuation of the strong CYP3A inhibitor, resume the previous dose. 63. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 64. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is required, decrease the cabozantinib dose by 40 mg/day (Cometriq) or 20 mg/day (Cabometyx). Resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuation of the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 65. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of calcitriol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 66. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 67. Posaconazole increases the levels of ceritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the ceritinib dose by approximately 33%. After discontinuation of the strong CYP3A inhibitor, resume the previous dose. 68. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 69. Posaconazole and citalopram both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 70. Posaconazole and clozapine both prolong the QTc interval and are contraindicated when used together. 71. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 72. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If co-administration is necessary, decrease the colchicine dose or frequency as recommended in prescribing information. 73. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of copanlisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
